**STEP 1: Vessel type.** The food sits on a flat white surface with a raised rim band and no inner wall or shadow, so it is a **square flat plate**.

**STEP 2: Vessel size.**
- a) Type: a large square dinner plate is typically 20-30 cm. The plate fills most of the frame, so I judge it a medium-large square plate, about 26 cm.
- b) Reference: the romanesco floret is about 4 cm, and roughly 5 florets span the plate's width (about 20 cm). This is lower than the type estimate, so I take the midpoint.
- Final width: about 24 cm, so area is about 576 cm².

**STEP 3: Food items.**
- **Turmeric rice:** covers about 20% of the plate (about 115 cm²). It is a flat, grainy layer about 0.7 cm thick on average. Volume is about 80 ml × 0.8 g/ml ≈ 65 g. I round up to 70 g, since it has some hidden base under the chicken.
- **Chicken:** covers about 12% (about 70 cm²). It is a thicker piece, about 1.2 cm at its peak and 0.8 cm on average. Volume is about 55 ml × 1.0 g/ml ≈ 55 g. I estimate 80 g because it is a dense, folded piece.
- **Cooked spinach:** covers about 15% (about 85 cm²), with an average thickness of about 0.7 cm. Volume is about 60 ml × 0.6 g/ml ≈ 36 g. I round up to 50 g to allow for leaves hidden under the chicken.
- **Romanesco broccoli:** covers about 8% (about 45 cm²). It is about 3 cm thick at the peak, averaging 1.5 cm. Volume is about 68 ml × 0.6 g/ml ≈ 40 g. I round up to 50 g.

**STEP 4: Hidden food.** The rice and greens likely extend under the chicken and broccoli, so I have already added a small allowance for them. No sauce is visible.

**STEP 5: kcal per 100 g, cooked.**
- Turmeric rice (cooked, with some oil): about 150 kcal/100 g.
- Chicken (cooked, with skin and herbs): about 200 kcal/100 g.
- Cooked spinach (with a little oil): about 40 kcal/100 g.
- Romanesco broccoli (cooked): about 35 kcal/100 g.

Totals: about 200 g of food, about 390 kcal.
